also.hook: Aidan Gomez studied mathematics and computer science as an undergraduate at the University of Toronto, working with Roger Grosse, before interning as a student researcher at Google Brain. There, working alongside Jakob Uszkoreit and other Google Brain researchers, he was one of eight co-authors of the 2017 paper Attention Is All You Need, which introduced the Transformer architecture that replaced recurrence and convolution with self-attention and went on to underpin most later large language models. He also co-authored the Reversible Residual Network (RevNet) paper on memory-efficient deep network training. He then pursued doctoral studies in machine learning at the University of Oxford, advised by Yarin Gal and Yee Whye Teh, while leading a research team at the nonprofit lab FOR.ai. In 2019 he co-founded Cohere in Toronto, where as CEO he has helped the company raise close to a billion dollars across four funding rounds and build enterprise-focused large language models.
also.name: Aidan Gomez

also.hook: Albert Gu is one of the two authors of Mamba, the 2023 paper that showed a state space model could match Transformer-quality language modeling while scaling linearly instead of quadratically with sequence length. The work built on his earlier S4 research from his Stanford PhD under Chris Re, and it gave the field its first credible architectural alternative to attention. Gu now holds both an academic and a commercial base for that idea, teaching as an Assistant Professor in Carnegie Mellon's Machine Learning Department while serving as Chief Scientist and Co-Founder at Cartesia, a startup applying state space models to real-time voice and audio AI. TIME named him to its 100 Most Influential People in AI in 2024 for that combination of research and applied work.
also.name: Albert Gu
also.moniker: Assistant Professor, Carnegie Mellon University, and Chief Scientist and Co-Founder, Cartesia

also.hook: Zhavoronkov built Insilico Medicine to prove that generative AI could do more than analyze biology, it could design new drug candidates outright, and Rentosertib, discovered and designed by Insilico's AI pipeline, became one of the first such molecules to reach human clinical trials.
also.name: Alex Zhavoronkov

also.hook: Andrej Karpathy has spent his career moving between building frontier neural networks and teaching other people how they work. He was a founding research scientist at OpenAI in 2015, then spent five years as Tesla's Director of AI leading the computer vision team behind Autopilot and Full Self-Driving. Along the way he designed and taught CS231n, Stanford's first deep learning course, and built a large public following through blog posts and YouTube lectures that walk through how language models are actually built. After a second stint at OpenAI and a run at his own AI education venture, Eureka Labs, he joined Anthropic's pretraining team in May 2026.
also.name: Andrej Karpathy
also.moniker: AI researcher, Anthropic, and OpenAI co-founder and former Tesla Director of AI

also.hook: Ng did more than any single figure to turn machine learning from a graduate-school subject into a skill anyone could learn online, while simultaneously building the industrial-scale infrastructure, Google Brain among it, that made deep learning practical at big-tech scale.
also.name: Andrew Ng
also.moniker: AI Educator and Deep Learning Pioneer

also.hook: Ashish Vaswani grew up partly in Oman before his family moved to Nagpur, India, when he was fifteen. He earned a bachelor's degree in computer science and engineering from Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra, worked briefly as a computer engineer in Delhi, then completed a master's degree and a PhD in computer science at the University of Southern California. He spent more than six years as a research scientist at Google Brain, and in 2017 he led the eight-author team, including Niki Parmar and Aidan Gomez, that published Attention Is All You Need, introducing the Transformer architecture that replaced recurrence and convolution with self-attention and became the base design for most later large language models. In April 2022 he co-founded Adept AI as chief scientist alongside Niki Parmar and David Luan, before leaving to co-found Essential AI with Parmar, where he now serves as CEO.
also.name: Ashish Vaswani

also.hook: Corinna Cortes earned a masters degree in physics from the University of Copenhagen before completing a PhD in computer science at the University of Rochester in 1993. She joined AT&T Bell Labs in 1989, where she spent more than a decade in the Adaptive Systems Research Group led by Larry Jackel. There she and Vladimir Vapnik developed the soft margin support vector machine, an extension that made support vector machines practical for real world classification problems with noisy, non separable data. Their 1995 paper on support vector networks became one of the most cited papers in machine learning. She later moved to Google, where she founded and now leads Google Research New York as a Vice President, overseeing large scale machine learning research across multiple international teams.
also.name: Corinna Cortes

also.hook: Daphne Koller earned undergraduate and masters degrees in computer science from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem before completing a PhD in computer science at Stanford University in 1993. She joined the Stanford faculty in 1995 and spent nearly two decades there as the Rajeev Motwani Professor of Computer Science, building a research program in probabilistic graphical models, a framework for reasoning under uncertainty that she detailed with Nir Friedman in the widely used textbook Probabilistic Graphical Models, Principles and Techniques. In 2012 she co-founded Coursera with fellow Stanford professor Andrew Ng, serving as co-CEO and president as the platform grew into one of the largest providers of massive open online courses. She later served as chief computing officer at Calico, an Alphabet company focused on aging research, before founding insitro in 2018, where she is CEO and applies machine learning and large scale biological data to drug discovery and development.
also.name: Daphne Koller
also.moniker: Founder and CEO, insitro, co-founder of Coursera

also.hook: Demis Hassabis showed an early talent for chess, reaching master strength as a teenager, before studying computer science at Cambridge and going on to design the video game Theme Park and lead AI programming on Black and White at Lionhead Studios. After running his own studio, Elixir Studios, he returned to academia and earned a PhD in cognitive neuroscience from University College London in 2009, studying memory and imagination. In 2010 he co-founded DeepMind with Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman to pursue general purpose learning systems, and Google acquired the company in 2014. Under his leadership DeepMind built landmark reinforcement learning systems, including AlphaGo, which defeated Go world champion Lee Sedol in 2016, and AlphaFold, which predicts the three dimensional structure of proteins from their amino acid sequences. Following a 2023 merger with Google Brain, he now leads the combined organization as co-founder and CEO of Google DeepMind. In 2024 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, shared with John Jumper and David Baker, for work on protein structure prediction, and was knighted for services to artificial intelligence.
also.name: Demis Hassabis

also.hook: Dolgov has been inside Google and Waymo's self-driving effort from its earliest days as a Google X project through its emergence as the first company to operate paid, fully driverless rides at commercial scale, rising from founding engineer to Co-CEO across that entire arc.
also.name: Dmitri Dolgov

also.hook: François Chollet created Keras, the deep learning library that became a default entry point into neural networks for millions of developers, while working as a Google engineer for close to a decade. In 2019 he published the ARC-AGI benchmark, arguing that measuring intelligence required tasks a system could not memorize its way through, and in 2024 he put a million dollars behind a public prize to beat it. He left Google in November 2024 to co-found Ndea with former Zapier president Mike Knoop, betting that program synthesis rather than further scaling is the more promising path toward general AI systems.
also.name: François Chollet

also.hook: Georgi Gerganov changed how large language models reach ordinary computers. Working from Sofia, Bulgaria, he built the ggml tensor library and then llama.cpp, a C and C++ inference engine that let Meta's LLaMA models run on a laptop through aggressive quantization instead of a data-center GPU. He founded ggml.ai in 2023 on pre-seed funding from Nat Friedman and Daniel Gross to sustain the project, and in February 2026 he and his team joined Hugging Face so llama.cpp would have long-term backing while staying fully open source.
also.name: Georgi Gerganov

also.hook: Illia Polosukhin worked as a machine learning engineer at Google, where he contributed to high level APIs for TensorFlow and worked on question answering systems used in Google Search. In 2017 he was one of eight coauthors of the paper Attention Is All You Need, which introduced the Transformer architecture built entirely on attention mechanisms and became the foundation for the large language models that followed. The next year he left Google and, together with Alexander Skidanov and other collaborators, began building a new blockchain protocol out of a small office in San Francisco. That project became NEAR Protocol, a sharded, proof of stake blockchain designed for usability and scalability, which launched its mainnet in 2020. Polosukhin continues to serve as a co-founder of NEAR, and has more recently worked on bringing large language model and AI agent technology into the NEAR ecosystem.
also.name: Illia Polosukhin

also.hook: Ilya Sutskever was born in Nizhny Novgorod, Russia, and moved with his family first to Israel and then to Canada, where he studied computer science at the University of Toronto under Geoffrey Hinton. In 2012 he co-authored the AlexNet paper with Alex Krizhevsky and Hinton, a deep convolutional network that sharply cut ImageNet classification error rates and helped launch the modern deep learning era. He followed this in 2014 with Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks, showing that a general encoder-decoder architecture could handle tasks like machine translation. In December 2015 he co-founded OpenAI, serving first as Research Director and later as Chief Scientist while the lab built its GPT model series. He left OpenAI in 2024 and co-founded Safe Superintelligence Inc with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy, a company dedicated to a single goal, building safe superintelligence, and became its CEO in mid-2025 after Gross departed.
also.name: Ilya Sutskever
also.moniker: Co-founder and CEO, Safe Superintelligence Inc.

also.hook: Jakob Uszkoreit grew up in Saarbrücken, Germany, and studied computer science and mathematics at the Berlin Institute of Technology, completing his master's degree summa cum laude in 2008. He joined Google that year after an earlier research internship, working first on data mining for Google Translate and later leading a semantic parsing team supporting Google Search and Assistant. In 2017 he co-authored Attention Is All You Need with colleagues at Google Brain, introducing the Transformer architecture that replaced recurrence and convolution with self-attention and became the foundation for most large language models built since. In 2021 he left Google to co-found Inceptive with biochemist Rhiju Das, applying deep learning models to the design of RNA-based medicines and pairing computational predictions with laboratory testing.
also.name: Jakob Uszkoreit

also.hook: Jakub Pachocki joined OpenAI in 2017 as a theoretical computer scientist fresh from a PhD in convex optimization, and rose to run the research programs behind some of the company's largest bets, including GPT-4 and the reinforcement-learning system that beat the world Dota 2 champions. In May 2024 OpenAI named him Chief Scientist, succeeding Ilya Sutskever, putting him in charge of the company's core research direction. He is credited with helping steer OpenAI toward reasoning models that work through problems step by step, an approach that produced systems scoring at gold-medal level on the International Mathematical Olympiad. Sam Altman has called him one of the strongest research minds at the company.
also.name: Jakub Pachocki

also.hook: Mustafa Suleyman was born in London in 1984 and studied at the University of Oxford. In 2010 he co-founded DeepMind, an artificial intelligence research lab that Google acquired in 2014, where he went on to lead applied AI and policy work. After leaving Google in 2019 and a period as a venture partner at Greylock, he co-founded Inflection AI in March 2022 with Reid Hoffman and Karen Simonyan, building the Pi personal assistant and the Inflection-2.5 model. In 2023 he published The Coming Wave, a book arguing that AI and synthetic biology pose a containment problem for governments and societies. In March 2024 he joined Microsoft as CEO of Microsoft AI, leading the Copilot consumer AI effort, and he has continued to write and speak about what he calls building humanist superintelligence.
also.name: Mustafa Suleyman

also.hook: Niki Parmar earned a bachelor's degree in information technology from the Pune Institute of Computer Technology in India, then a master's degree in computer science from the University of Southern California. She joined Google in 2015 as an engineer and research scientist, working on end to end deep learning systems for natural language processing. In 2017, reportedly the youngest member of her team and the only one without a PhD, she co-authored Attention Is All You Need, the paper that introduced the Transformer architecture. She spent close to seven years at Google before co-founding Adept AI Labs in 2022 as Chief Technology Officer, building enterprise workflow automation tools, and then co-founding Essential AI in 2023 to build full stack AI products for automating data processing, with backing from Google and Nvidia. She has since also worked as a member of technical staff at Anthropic on reliable and interpretable AI systems.
also.name: Niki Parmar

also.hook: Noam Shazeer joined Google in 2000, where he first worked on improving the search engine's spelling correction and helped develop the PHIL algorithm that became central to Google AdSense. Over the next two decades he moved into deep learning, co-authoring a paper on sparsely gated mixture of experts models in 2016 and then, in 2017, co-authoring Attention Is All You Need, where he designed the multi-head attention mechanism at the core of the Transformer. He went on to create Mesh-TensorFlow in 2018 for training large Transformers across many machines, co-authored the T5 model in 2019, and contributed to Google's LaMDA dialogue system. In 2021 he left Google to co-found Character.AI with Daniel De Freitas, serving as its CEO and building one of the first consumer chatbots built on Transformer technology. In August 2024 he returned to Google as part of a licensing deal with Character.AI, rejoining Google DeepMind's research team, and later co-led development of the Gemini model as Vice President of Engineering before departing for OpenAI in June 2026.
also.name: Noam Shazeer

also.hook: Raquel Urtasun is a computer scientist and entrepreneur who has spent her career at the intersection of computer vision, robotics, and self driving technology. She earned her PhD in computer science from the Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne in 2006, then completed postdoctoral research at MIT and UC Berkeley before joining the Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago as an assistant professor. She later became a Canada Research Chair in Machine Learning and Computer Vision at the University of Toronto, where she remains a full professor and is a co-founder of the Vector Institute for AI. From 2017 to 2021 she served as Chief Scientist and Head of Research and Development at Uber's Advanced Technologies Group in Toronto, leading self driving vehicle research. After leaving Uber, she founded Waabi, a company building AI first software for autonomous trucks and robotaxis, where she serves as Founder and CEO.
also.name: Raquel Urtasun

also.hook: Rodney Brooks trained in pure mathematics at Flinders University in his native Australia before earning a PhD in computer science from Stanford in 1981. After research positions at Carnegie Mellon, MIT and Stanford, he joined the MIT faculty in 1984 and later directed the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory and then the Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. His 1986 paper describing the subsumption architecture argued that intelligent robot behavior could emerge from layered, reactive control systems rather than centralized symbolic planning, a challenge to the AI orthodoxy of the time that helped found the field of behavior-based robotics. He put that thinking into commercial practice by co-founding iRobot in 1990 with Colin Angle and Helen Greiner, whose Roomba vacuum became one of the first robots to reach mass consumer markets. In 2008 he founded Heartland Robotics, later renamed Rethink Robotics, to build the Baxter and Sawyer collaborative robots for factory work, and in 2019 he founded Robust.AI to continue work on practical, everyday robotics.
also.name: Rodney Brooks
also.moniker: Roboticist and co-founder of iRobot and Rethink Robotics

also.hook: Thrun proved autonomous driving was possible by winning DARPA's toughest robotics prize, then built the Google program that turned that proof into Waymo, the industry's leading self-driving company, while separately co-founding Udacity to bring university-grade technical education online.
also.name: Sebastian Thrun
also.moniker: Founder of Google's Self-Driving Car Project and Udacity

also.hook: O'Reilly has spent four decades doing the same thing under different names: spotting a technology shift before the industry has language for it, then naming it. 'Open source' and 'Web 2.0' both trace to conferences he convened, and his publishing house has been the technical-literacy backbone for the programmers who built the modern internet, and now AI.
also.name: Tim O'Reilly
also.moniker: Publisher Who Named Web 2.0 and the Open Source Movement

also.hook: Gruber built a career in academic knowledge-representation research before co-founding Siri, whose acquisition by Apple in 2010 put conversational AI into hundreds of millions of pockets years before ChatGPT made the category mainstream, and he has argued ever since for AI designed to amplify human intelligence rather than substitute for it.
also.name: Tom Gruber

profiles.hook: Germanidis co-founded the generative-video company Runway in 2018 and served as its CTO for over seven years before becoming Co-CEO in 2026. Before Runway he worked in machine learning and computer vision at IBM Research and as a backend engineer at Zocdoc, Chartbeat, and Quantcast.

profiles.hook: Gilman's brand philosophy, that the best brands make people feel something real, was forged across twenty-five years of payments and fintech marketing where the product is inherently invisible. She helped grow Zelle past a trillion dollars in transactions and launched Paze from scratch to a David Ogilvy Silver Award. Her public view on AI is clear: it is a tool for freeing humans to do what humans do best, and trust, judgment, and creativity remain at the heart of great brands.

profiles.hook: Andrew Feldman has built two companies around the same conviction, that general-purpose processors are the wrong tool for specialized workloads. He first proved it with SeaMicro, a microserver startup he founded in 2007 that AMD acquired in 2012 for roughly 334 million dollars. He then co-founded Cerebras Systems in 2015 to apply the same logic to AI, building the Wafer-Scale Engine, a single chip roughly the size of a dinner plate designed specifically to keep AI training data close to compute instead of shuttling it between separate processors. As Cerebras CEO, Feldman has positioned wafer-scale computing as an alternative to clusters of GPUs for large-scale AI training and inference.

profiles.hook: Arthur Mensch spent two and a half years researching large language models at Google DeepMind before deciding, alongside longtime friends Guillaume Lample and Timothee Lacroix, that a European lab could compete at the frontier while keeping its models open. The three co-founded Mistral AI in Paris in April 2023, and Mensch has run the company as CEO since, positioning it as an open-weight counterweight to closed labs in the US. He holds a doctorate in machine learning from Paris-Saclay University, following earlier study at Ecole Polytechnique and Telecom Paris, and in 2025 was named a Knight of the French National Order of Merit.

He now sits on the board of Nikola Motor Company, the autonomous and electric truck maker, while running his own holding company, Voltava.

profiles.hook: C.C. Wei leads the company that manufactures most of the world's advanced AI chips. He joined TSMC in 1998 after earlier engineering roles at Texas Instruments, ST Microelectronics, and Chartered Semiconductor, and spent the next quarter century rising through business development and operating roles before becoming President and Co-CEO in 2013, sole CEO in 2018, and Chairman and CEO in 2024. Under his leadership TSMC's advanced process nodes have become the manufacturing bottleneck and enabler for the generative AI buildout, supplying the chips behind most leading GPUs and AI accelerators. He holds a PhD in electrical engineering from Yale and has repeatedly told investors that AI-driven demand for TSMC's most advanced capacity remains structurally strong even as supply stays tight.

profiles.hook: Chris Olah helped invent the field of mechanistic interpretability, the effort to reverse engineer the internal workings of neural networks into algorithms a person can actually read. He built that career without a college degree, funding it instead with a Thiel Fellowship, then spent years at Google Brain visualizing what neural networks see before leading interpretability research at OpenAI. In 2021 he co-founded Anthropic and now leads its interpretability work, publishing the Transformer Circuits research thread that tries to map language models circuit by circuit. He also co-founded Distill, a journal built around explaining machine learning clearly rather than tersely. In 2026 he took that argument to the Vatican, telling an audience beside Pope Leo XIV that AI's governance problems cannot be left to computer scientists alone.
profiles.name: Chris Olah
profiles.moniker: Co-founder and Interpretability Lead, Anthropic

profiles.hook: Christopher Ré runs Stanford's Hazy Research lab, which has spent more than a decade turning ideas about data quality and hardware efficiency into companies. His early work on DeepDive, a system for pulling structured facts out of unstructured dark data, won him a MacArthur Fellowship in 2015. He later co-founded Snorkel AI to make labeling training data programmatic instead of manual, and Together AI, alongside collaborators including Tri Dao, Ce Zhang and Percy Liang, to build infrastructure for training and running open foundation models. Along the way his lab's systems work on hardware-aware training has fed directly into how modern language models are trained and served at scale.

profiles.hook: Clement Delangue co-founded Hugging Face in 2016 with Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf, originally as a chatbot app, and steered it into the default home for sharing open-source AI models and datasets. Before that he worked in product management at Moodstocks, a computer vision startup that Google acquired the same year Hugging Face began. As CEO he built a platform that by September 2026 hosted more than 3 million models and 500,000 datasets used by more than 18 million developers. That same month he agreed to sell the company to Nvidia for roughly 12.9 billion dollars, negotiating to keep Hugging Face open across clouds, frameworks and chip vendors rather than tied to Nvidia's hardware alone.

profiles.hook: Daniela Amodei runs the day-to-day operations of Anthropic, the AI safety company she co-founded with her brother Dario in 2021 after both left OpenAI. Her path there ran through Capitol Hill and international development work before she spent years at Stripe, helping grow the company from about 40 employees to more than 300 and later working on platform risk with engineers, ML specialists and lawyers. At OpenAI she focused on AI safety and policy before deciding to help start a company built around that idea from the ground up. As President, she describes her job as taking the technical safety vision of Anthropic's research leadership and turning it into concrete operating norms for the company.

profiles.hook: Dario Amodei trained as a physicist, earning a Ph.D. in biophysics from Princeton as a Hertz Fellow before moving into machine learning at Baidu, briefly at Google Brain, and then at OpenAI. As OpenAI's Vice President of Research, he set research direction, led the teams that built GPT-2 and GPT-3, and helped pioneer reinforcement learning from human feedback. In 2021 he left to co-found Anthropic, where as CEO he has pushed the idea that AI safety and frontier capability can be built together rather than traded off. He argues that case publicly too, from his 2024 essay Machines of Loving Grace on AI's potential upside to a 2025 New York Times op-ed calling for basic transparency rules on frontier AI development.

profiles.hook: David Holz built the generative image tool that made AI art a mainstream habit. Before Midjourney, he spent more than a decade as co-founder and CTO of Leap Motion, developing hand-tracking hardware that never found its mass market. He founded Midjourney in 2021 as an independent research lab, kept it privately held, and grew it past 20 million users without taking outside investment. He describes the project as an attempt to expand human imagination rather than to build imaginative machines, and Disney and Universal's 2025 copyright lawsuit against the company shows how far that project now reaches into the rest of the entertainment industry.

A former hedge fund manager, he positioned Stability AI as a counterweight to closed AI labs, backing open releases rather than gating models behind an API. He resigned as CEO and left the board in March 2024, saying he wanted to pursue decentralized AI outside a single company, and by late 2024 Stability AI confirmed he no longer had any control over it.

profiles.hook: Jared Kaplan built his early career as a theoretical physicist, holding a PhD from Harvard and a faculty position at Johns Hopkins studying quantum gravity and conformal field theory. Starting in 2018 he turned that background toward machine learning, working on how language model performance scales with compute, data and parameters, research his own university describes as feeding into GPT-3. In 2021 he co-founded Anthropic and became its Chief Science Officer, leading the technical research behind models like Claude and methods such as Constitutional AI. He still holds his Johns Hopkins physics appointment alongside his role at Anthropic.

profiles.hook: Jensen Huang founded NVIDIA in 1993 and has run it continuously ever since, first as a graphics chip maker for PC gaming and later as the dominant supplier of the GPUs that power modern AI training and inference. He holds a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and a master's from Stanford, and worked at LSI Logic and Advanced Micro Devices before starting NVIDIA. Under his leadership the company introduced the GPU in 1999, a product line that eventually became the core infrastructure of the generative AI boom. He has since been recognized with engineering's biggest honors, including a share of the 2025 Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering and the 2026 IEEE Medal of Honor.

profiles.hook: Jim Keller has spent four decades moving between the biggest names in semiconductors, leaving a distinct architecture behind at each stop. He led design of AMD's Zen microarchitecture, the chip line credited with reviving the company's competitiveness against Intel, and earlier led the engineering behind Apple's A4 and A5 mobile processors after Apple acquired P.A. Semi. He later ran Autopilot hardware engineering at Tesla and Silicon Engineering at Intel before moving into AI accelerator chips. He is now CEO of Tenstorrent and has also co-founded Atomic Semi, a startup building small-scale chip fabs.

profiles.hook: Jonathan Ross started what became Google's Tensor Processing Unit as an internal side project, then left to found Groq in 2016, building a chip architecture designed purely for AI inference. Groq's language processing units made the company one of the most closely watched hardware challengers to Nvidia. In December 2025 Nvidia took a non-exclusive license to Groq's technology and hired Ross along with most of Groq's engineering team, a deal that returned billions of dollars to Groq's shareholders and moved its founder inside the company his chips were built to compete with. Ross now works at Nvidia as its chief software architect, and has spoken candidly about the leadership mistakes he made running Groq for nearly a decade.

profiles.hook: Julien Chaumond co-founded Hugging Face in 2016 and has served as its chief technology officer since, building the technical infrastructure, the Hub, the Transformers library, and the huggingface_hub client, that turned the company into the default distribution point for open machine learning models. Before Hugging Face he ran two earlier startups, Prodcast and the reading platform Glose, and advised the French Deputy Minister for Digital Affairs. He describes Hugging Face's approach as belonging to its user community rather than standing apart from it, a framing that has shaped the company's open-source strategy as its Hub scaled to millions of hosted models and datasets.

profiles.hook: Lisa Su has led AMD since October 2014, combining an electrical-engineering research background with semiconductor operations experience to turn the company from a distant also-ran into a primary supplier of AI accelerator hardware. Her MI300 and MI400 series GPUs gave large AI labs and cloud providers a credible second source of high-end accelerators alongside Nvidia. Su holds three degrees in electrical engineering from MIT and built her career through technical and general-management roles at Texas Instruments, IBM, and Freescale Semiconductor before joining AMD in 2012. She was named Time's CEO of the Year in 2024 and continues to set AMD's AI infrastructure roadmap, from CES keynotes to plans for trillion-parameter-scale training clusters.

profiles.hook: Mark Chen has been at OpenAI since 2018, moving from quantitative trading into leading some of the company's most visible research programs. He co-led the team that built DALL-E, directed the vision work that gave GPT-4 its multimodal capabilities, and oversaw Codex, the model behind GitHub Copilot. In March 2025 OpenAI named him Chief Research Officer, a role focused on integrating research and product development so new capabilities move into deployment faster. He also coaches the USA Computing Olympiad team, a pastime that tracks with his own path through competitive mathematics and computer science at MIT.

profiles.hook: Robin Rombach is the lead author of the Latent Diffusion Models paper produced with the CompVis group at LMU Munich, the research that became the technical basis for Stable Diffusion. After a physics degree at Heidelberg and a PhD at LMU Munich, he continued the work as Research Director at Stability AI before leaving in 2024. In August 2024 he co-founded Black Forest Labs with two of his Latent Diffusion co-authors, Patrick Esser and Andreas Blattmann, releasing the FLUX.1 image model on launch day. He now runs Black Forest Labs as CEO from labs in Freiburg and San Francisco, and in 2026 spoke at the G7 alongside heads of state to argue for keeping frontier visual AI development open.

profiles.hook: Soumith Chintala spent eleven years at Facebook and Meta building the infrastructure researchers actually use, and in 2016 that work became PyTorch, a framework Meta's own engineering blog credits him with co-creating. PyTorch went from a research tool to the default choice for training large language models and most of the vision and generative models that followed it. In January 2026 he left the company where he built his career to become Chief Technology Officer at Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab, taking on AI infrastructure and research at a new frontier lab. He also holds an affiliation at NYU, the university where he earned his master's degree under Yann LeCun, working there on home robotics with Lerrel Pinto.

profiles.hook: Thomas Wolf trained as a physicist, not a computer scientist, earning a PhD in statistical and quantum physics before spending five years as a patent attorney in Paris. He taught himself deep learning in 2015 and 2016 and used it to co-found Hugging Face, then helped build the Transformers library that became the standard interface to pretrained language models across the field. As the company's Chief Science Officer he has also driven its open-science side, including the BigScience workshop that produced the BLOOM model. In September 2026, Hugging Face agreed to be acquired by NVIDIA in a deal reported near thirteen billion dollars, a turn Wolf described on X as an outcome nobody at the company anticipated back in 2016.

profiles.hook: Tim Dettmers built his career on the wager that making large models run on far less hardware would open up who gets to do AI research at all. His PhD work at the University of Washington, advised by Luke Zettlemoyer, produced LLM.int8() in 2022 and then QLoRA in 2023, a method that let a 65 billion parameter language model be fine-tuned on a single 48 gigabyte GPU. He maintains bitsandbytes, the open-source quantization library those methods run on, and in 2024 he became an Assistant Professor at Carnegie Mellon University while continuing as a Research Scientist at the Allen Institute for AI. His own faculty page describes his focus as making foundation models accessible to researchers and practitioners by reducing their resource requirements.

profiles.hook: Timothée Lacroix worked on Meta's LLaMA language models as a researcher at Facebook AI Research before leaving in 2023 to co-found Mistral AI with Arthur Mensch and Guillaume Lample. As Chief Technology Officer he leads the Paris-based company's research and technical direction, the work behind models like Mistral Large and the Le Chat assistant. Mistral positioned itself from the outset as a European counterweight to closed, US-based AI labs, releasing open-weight models such as Mistral 7B alongside its commercial offerings. Lacroix trained as a computer scientist at the Ecole Normale Superieure and holds a doctorate tied to the University of Paris-Est.

profiles.hook: Tri Dao's PhD work at Stanford, co-advised by Christopher Re and Stefano Ermon, produced FlashAttention, a fast, memory-efficient attention algorithm that cut a Transformer's memory use from quadratic to linear in sequence length. Presented at NeurIPS in 2022 and later extended in FlashAttention-2 and FlashAttention-3, it became a piece of infrastructure that most large language models now train and run on. He joined Together AI as a co-founder and Chief Scientist around the time he finished his PhD, and is also an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at Princeton University, where he leads the Dao AI Lab.

profiles.hook: Yangqing Jia was still a PhD student at UC Berkeley when he built Caffe, one of the first deep learning frameworks to open source its full code and model zoo, and it became a standard tool for computer vision research for several years. He carried that pattern through a string of AI infrastructure roles, co-creating Google's Inception architecture at Google Brain, building Facebook's internal AI platform and co-creating Caffe2 and ONNX there, then running Alibaba Cloud's computing platform and its DAMO Academy systems lab. He founded Lepton AI in 2023, sold it to NVIDIA in 2025, left NVIDIA in mid-2026 over the company's decision not to open source the platform, and that July launched Intent Lab, an autonomous software engineering startup, with several former Lepton AI colleagues.
